events.title: The 2023 price spike
events.text: Heat, then heavy rain and pest damage cut supply across the tomato belt. Retail prices passed ₹200/kg in several cities, and the government arranged subsidised sales.

events.title: The crash after the spike
events.text: High prices drew in a lot of planting. When that crop arrived together, prices fell sharply and some farmers did not recover picking costs.

events.title: Unseasonal rain in the south
events.text: Heavy rain in Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka damaged standing crops and pushed prices up at a time they are usually moderate.

predict.title: Mandi AI
predict.intro: A 4-week price estimate for Madanapalle, built from seasonal patterns and the recent trend.
predict.how: It takes the usual seasonal pattern from ten years of monthly prices, then adds the trend from the last 8 weeks and lets that trend fade over time. The shaded band widens the further ahead it looks. It cannot foresee sudden events like floods or pest outbreaks, so use it as one signal alongside what you hear at the mandi.

grow.title: How to Grow Tomatoes
grow.intro: From choosing land to selling at the mandi, in 11 steps.

steps.title: Choose land and test the soil
steps.text: Pick well-drained loam with a pH of about 6 to 7. Avoid fields that grew tomato, chilli, brinjal or potato last season. Get a soil test through your local agriculture office.

steps.title: Choose a variety and buy seed
steps.text: Match the variety to your season and to what buyers at your mandi want. Buy from a licensed dealer, and keep the bill and the seed packet.

steps.title: Raise the nursery
steps.text: Sow in protrays or raised beds and cover with insect-proof net. Seedlings are ready in about 25 to 30 days, at 4 to 5 true leaves.

steps.title: Prepare land, beds and mulch
steps.text: Plough well, mix in compost, and form raised beds. Plastic mulch saves water, keeps weeds down and helps fruit stay clean.

steps.title: Set up drip irrigation
steps.text: Lay drip lines along the beds and flush them before planting. Drip saves water and lets you feed the crop through the lines. Ask about subsidy first.

steps.title: Transplant
steps.text: Plant in the evening into moist beds, roughly 60 to 90 cm between rows and 45 to 60 cm between plants. Water straight after, and replace any that die within a week.

steps.title: Stake and tie
steps.text: Put up stakes and wires about 3 to 4 weeks after planting. Tie plants as they grow, so fruit stays off the soil and spray reaches the leaves.

steps.title: Follow a fertilizer schedule
steps.text: Base the plan on your soil test. Give a basal dose, then split nitrogen and potash through the crop by drip. Fruit set needs steady calcium, boron and water.

steps.title: Watch for pests and disease
steps.text: Walk the field at least twice a week. Use yellow sticky traps and pheromone traps, remove infected plants early, and spray only when needed.

steps.title: Harvest and grade
steps.text: First picking is usually 60 to 70 days after transplanting. Pick at the colour your buyer wants, every 3 to 4 days, in the cool of the day. Sort by size and quality.

steps.title: Pack and sell
steps.text: Pack into clean crates without overfilling. Reach the mandi before the auction starts, and check today's prices first so you can pick the right market.

pests.title: Pest and Disease Guide
pests.intro: How to spot the common problems early, and what to do.
pests.safety: Confirm the problem and the dose with your local agriculture officer or Krishi Vigyan Kendra. Follow the product label, wear protection, and respect the waiting time before harvest.

leafCurl.name: Leaf curl virus
leafCurl.symptoms: Leaves curl upward and turn small and yellow. Plants stay stunted and bear little fruit.
leafCurl.identify: New growth looks bunched and leathery, often with whiteflies under the leaves.
leafCurl.prevention: Use resistant varieties, net the nursery, control whitefly, and clear weeds around the field.
leafCurl.treatment: There is no cure. Remove infected plants early and manage the whitefly that spreads it.

earlyBlight.name: Early blight
earlyBlight.symptoms: Brown spots appear on older leaves first, and leaves dry and drop.
earlyBlight.identify: Spots have rings like a target, often with a yellow edge.
earlyBlight.prevention: Rotate crops, stake plants for airflow, and water by drip instead of overhead.
earlyBlight.treatment: Remove affected leaves. Spray a recommended fungicide such as mancozeb as per the label.

lateBlight.name: Late blight
lateBlight.symptoms: Dark, water-soaked patches spread quickly on leaves, stems and fruit in cool, wet weather.
lateBlight.identify: White mould shows under leaves in humid mornings. Fruit gets firm brown patches.
lateBlight.prevention: Avoid dense planting, keep leaves dry, and watch closely after rain.
lateBlight.treatment: Act fast: spray a recommended systemic fungicide before and just after wet spells, as per the label.

fruitBorer.name: Fruit borer
fruitBorer.symptoms: Round holes in fruit, with droppings around them. Fruit rots and cannot be sold.
fruitBorer.identify: Green to brown caterpillars feed with half their body inside the fruit.
fruitBorer.prevention: Set pheromone traps, grow marigold as a trap crop, and collect damaged fruit.
fruitBorer.treatment: Use NPV or Bt sprays when young larvae appear. Use a recommended insecticide if damage grows.

whitefly.name: Whitefly
whitefly.symptoms: Leaves turn yellow and sticky, and black mould grows on the honeydew.
whitefly.identify: Tiny white insects fly up when you shake the plant.
whitefly.prevention: Use yellow sticky traps, net the nursery, and avoid planting next to infested crops.
whitefly.treatment: Spray neem oil early. Change the insecticide group between sprays so resistance does not build.

wilt.name: Wilt
wilt.symptoms: Plants droop suddenly and die, often in patches, even with moist soil.
wilt.identify: Cut the stem and place it in clear water. Milky threads point to bacterial wilt, and brown inner tissue points to fusarium.
wilt.prevention: Use resistant varieties or grafted plants, improve drainage, and rotate with non-solanaceous crops.
wilt.treatment: Remove and destroy wilted plants. Add Trichoderma with compost, and avoid moving soil between fields.

schemes.title: Government Schemes
schemes.intro: Support that tomato farmers can apply for. Amounts change, so always check the official site.
schemes.note: Summaries only, and rules change. Your Rythu Seva Kendra or agriculture office can confirm current terms.

drip.name: Drip irrigation subsidy
drip.gives: Central support under PMKSY Per Drop More Crop, usually 55% of unit cost for small and marginal farmers and 45% for others. States may add more.
drip.who: Farmers with land records, applying through the state micro-irrigation programme.

pmfby.name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana
pmfby.gives: Crop insurance against natural calamities, pests and disease. The farmer's premium for horticultural crops is capped at 5%, where the crop is notified.
pmfby.who: Farmers growing notified crops in notified areas, including tenant farmers.

pmkisan.name: PM-KISAN
pmkisan.gives: ₹6,000 a year, paid directly to bank accounts in three instalments.
pmkisan.who: Landholding farmer families, subject to exclusion rules such as income tax payers.

midh.name: Horticulture mission (MIDH)
midh.gives: Assistance for planting material, protected cultivation, mulching, pack houses and cold storage.
midh.who: Farmers, farmer groups and FPOs, through the state horticulture department.

greens.name: Operation Greens
greens.gives: Support for tomato, onion and potato value chains, including help with storage and transport during gluts.
greens.who: FPOs, processors, traders and cooperatives, as per scheme rules.

enam.name: e-NAM
enam.gives: Online trading platform linking mandis, so more buyers can bid on your produce.
enam.who: Farmers registered at a mandi that has joined e-NAM.

faq.a: Many farmers plant at the same time, often after a year of high prices. When that crop ripens together, arrivals jump. Tomatoes cannot be stored for long, so farmers must sell even at low prices.

faq.q: Why do prices suddenly shoot up?
faq.a: Heavy rain, heat waves or pest attacks can wipe out supply across a whole region in a few weeks. Because the crop takes months to replace, prices stay high until new fields come in.
It is the group of major growing areas that supply the country. In the south, it includes Madanapalle and Chittoor in Andhra Pradesh and Kolar in Karnataka. Nashik and Pune are key in Maharashtra.
Its market is known as one of Asia's largest for tomatoes. Its climate suits the crop, and traders from across India buy here.

learn.storiesNote: Illustrative examples written for this site, not real people. Real stories can replace them, with each farmer's permission.

stories.name: Lakshmi (example)
stories.text: After losing a crop to leaf curl, Lakshmi switched to a resistant hybrid and a netted nursery. Fewer plants failed, and picking lasted longer.

stories.name: Ramesh (example)
stories.text: Ramesh began comparing nearby mandis after transport costs. On some days the farther market paid more, and on others it did not, so he now checks first.

stories.name: Fathima (example)
stories.text: Fathima spread her planting over three dates. When prices fell in one week, her later picking still caught better rates.
